Resolves a workspaceRoot, returns [] if it does not exist or is not a directory (safe default) - Uses getAllFiles(workspaceRoot) to walk files - Regex-scans for `@story ` in file contents - Uses isUnsafeStoryPath + enforceProjectBoundary to avoid path traversal / absolute-path issues and to stay inside project boundaries - tests/perf/maintenance-large-workspace.test.ts – REQ-MAINT-DETECT perf test: detectStaleAnnotations returns >0 stale entries and completes well under 5 seconds on a large synthetic workspace,Core update & batch functionality (REQ-MAINT-UPDATE, REQ-MAINT-BATCH): - Implementation: src/maintenance/update.ts - export function updateAnnotationReferences(codebasePath, oldPath, newPath): number - Validates that codebasePath exists and is a directory; returns 0 otherwise - Uses getAllFiles to walk files - Builds a regex `(@story\s*)${escapedOldPath}` and only replaces the path portion, preserving surrounding content/formatting - Writes file only if content actually changed; counts replacements - Implementation: src/maintenance/batch.ts - export function batchUpdateAnnotations(codebasePath, mappings): number - Iterates mappings and calls updateAnnotationReferences for each, summing counts - export function verifyAnnotations(codebasePath): boolean - Uses detectStaleAnnotations and returns true iff no stale annotations remain - Tests: - tests/maintenance/update.test.ts – verifies updateAnnotationReferences returns 0 when there are no matches - tests/maintenance/batch.test.ts – verifies: - batchUpdateAnnotations returns 0 with empty mappings - verifyAnnotations returns true when a matching .story.md file exists for the annotated story - tests/perf/maintenance-large-workspace.test.ts – verifies: - updateAnnotationReferences updates >0 annotations and runs under a generous time budget - batchUpdateAnnotations updates >=2 annotations and runs under budget,Reporting & verification functionality (REQ-MAINT-VERIFY, REQ-MAINT-REPORT, REQ-MAINT-SAFE): - Implementation: src/maintenance/report.ts - export function generateMaintenanceReport(codebasePath): string - Uses detectStaleAnnotations - Returns "" when there are no stale annotations (explicit safe no-op signal) - Otherwise returns a newline-separated list of stale story paths - Implementation: src/maintenance/batch.ts - verifyAnnotations (above) provides simple boolean verification over detectStaleAnnotations - Tests: - tests/maintenance/report.test.ts – verifies: - generateMaintenanceReport returns empty string when no stale annotations - generateMaintenanceReport returns a report containing the stale story name when configured with a missing story - tests/maintenance/batch.test.ts – verifies verifyAnnotations returns true when annotations and story files are consistent - tests/perf/maintenance-large-workspace.test.ts – verifies generateMaintenanceReport returns a non-empty string and runs under 5 seconds,CLI integration and user experience (REQ-MAINT-DETECT, REQ-MAINT-VERIFY, REQ-MAINT-REPORT, REQ-MAINT-UPDATE, REQ-MAINT-BATCH, REQ-MAINT-SAFE): - Switches on subcommand to call handleDetect/handleVerify/handleReport/handleUpdate - For unknown commands, prints an error plus help and returns EXIT_USAGE (2) - Wraps handlers in a try/catch; on error logs `traceability-maint failed: ` and returns EXIT_USAGE - traceability.notes:
All functional requirements and acceptance criteria for 009.0-DEV-MAINTENANCE-TOOLS appear fully implemented: - Core functionality is present: detection of stale @story references, per-path updates, batch updates, and verification, exposed both as programmatic APIs and via the traceability-maint CLI. - Quality and safety are addressed: operations only touch @story paths, preserve surrounding content, short-circuit on invalid roots, respect project boundaries, and are covered by performance tests on large synthetic workspaces. - Integration is in place: the maintenance tools are exported from src/maintenance/index.ts, wired into the published CLI via package.json, and reuse existing story reference utilities from the plugin. - User experience is validated: CLI commands provide clear text output, JSON modes for automation, a detailed help message, specific exit codes, and tests explicitly confirm the UX behavior. - Error handling is robust: non-existent roots, invalid flags, permission errors, unsafe story paths, missing parameters, and unknown commands are handled gracefully with safe defaults and informative messages. - Documentation exists and is user-facing in README.md with concrete examples and references to deeper API docs.
Given the breadth of implementation, extensive targeted tests tied to this story, and a fully passing test suite, this story is assessed as PASSED.
